evidence: The paper applies a forward feature selection algorithm with five different model types including random forests. Random forest is used only for comparison; the paper reports that "The random forest model selected all variables 100% of the time during the training process" but selects gradient boosting machine (GBM) as the top-performing algorithm based on RMSE. Variable rankings are determined via AIC-based model selection ("AIC is used for ranking the maximum likelihood population effects models") and model convergence across MLPE and LCTA frameworks. The conclusion states: "Multiple statistical approaches converged on the conclusion that wolverine genetic connectivity across western North America was positively associated with forest cover and negatively associated with human disturbance."
